entries: A prime number is a whole number greater than 1 whose only factors are 1 and itself, for example 2, 3, 5, 7, 11 and 13. 2 is the only even prime number.
A composite number is a whole number greater than 1 that has more than two factors, for example 4, 6, 8, 9 and 12.
No. 1 is neither prime nor composite, because it has only one factor (itself).
What is the smallest prime number?
The smallest prime number is 2. It is also the only even prime number.
Natural numbers are the counting numbers: 1, 2, 3, 4, … (Some books include 0.)
Whole numbers are 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, … — the natural numbers together with zero.
Integers are all whole numbers and their negatives: … −3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3 …
A rational number can be written as p/q, where p and q are integers and q ≠ 0, for example 1/2, −3, 0.75. Its decimal either ends or repeats.
An irrational number cannot be written as a fraction p/q. Its decimal goes on forever without repeating, for example √2, √3 and π.
Real numbers are all rational and irrational numbers together — every point on the number line.
An even number divides by 2 exactly: 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, … It ends in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8.
An odd number leaves remainder 1 when divided by 2: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, … It ends in 1, 3, 5, 7 or 9.
A factor of a number divides it exactly. For example, the factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12.
A multiple of a number is that number times a whole number. For example, multiples of 4 are 4, 8, 12, 16, …
HCF (Highest Common Factor), also called GCD, is the largest number that divides two or more numbers exactly. HCF of 12 and 18 is 6.
LCM (Lowest Common Multiple) is the smallest number that is a multiple of two or more numbers. LCM of 4 and 6 is 12.
What is the relation between HCF and LCM?
For two numbers a and b: HCF × LCM = a × b.
A fraction shows part of a whole, written as numerator/denominator, like 3/4 (3 parts out of 4 equal parts).
A proper fraction has a numerator smaller than its denominator, like 2/5.
An improper fraction has a numerator greater than or equal to its denominator, like 7/4. It can be written as a mixed number: 1 3/4.
A mixed fraction (mixed number) has a whole number and a proper fraction, like 2 1/3. It equals 7/3.
Equivalent fractions have the same value, like 1/2 = 2/4 = 3/6. Multiply or divide the top and bottom by the same number.
A percentage is a number out of 100. 25% means 25 out of 100, or 1/4.
A ratio compares two quantities of the same kind, written a : b. For example, 2 boys to 3 girls is 2 : 3.
A proportion says two ratios are equal: a : b = c : d, which means a × d = b × c.
A square number is a number times itself: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49, 64, 81, 100, …
A cube number is a number multiplied by itself three times: 1, 8, 27, 64, 125, …
The square root of a number is the value that, multiplied by itself, gives the number. √49 = 7 because 7 × 7 = 49.
An exponent (power) tells how many times to multiply a number by itself. In 2⁵, 5 is the exponent: 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 32.
What are the laws of exponents?
aᵐ × aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ; aᵐ ÷ aⁿ = aᵐ⁻ⁿ; (aᵐ)ⁿ = aᵐⁿ; (ab)ⁿ = aⁿbⁿ; a⁰ = 1; a⁻ⁿ = 1/aⁿ.
What is anything to the power 0?
Any non-zero number to the power 0 equals 1: a⁰ = 1.
BODMAS gives the order of operations: Brackets, Orders (powers and roots), Division and Multiplication (left to right), Addition and Subtraction (left to right). Also called PEMDAS.
In maths, a variable is a letter such as x or y that stands for an unknown or changing number.
An equation says two expressions are equal, using =, like 2x + 3 = 11.
A linear equation has the variable only to the power 1, like 3x + 2 = 8. Its graph is a straight line.
A quadratic equation has the form ax² + bx + c = 0 with a ≠ 0. It has at most two solutions.
For ax² + bx + c = 0: x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) / 2a. The discriminant b² − 4ac tells the kind of roots: positive → two real roots, zero → one repeated root, negative → no real roots.
A polynomial is an expression with variables and whole-number powers, like 3x² − 2x + 5. Its degree is the highest power.
A coefficient is the number multiplying a variable. In 7x², the coefficient is 7.
In maths, a function gives exactly one output for each input, like f(x) = 2x + 1.
A set is a well-defined collection of objects, written in braces, like A = {1, 2, 3}.
What is the union of sets?
The union A ∪ B contains every element that is in A or B (or both).
What is the intersection of sets?
The intersection A ∩ B contains the elements that are in both A and B.
The mean (average) is the sum of the values divided by how many values there are.
The median is the middle value when the values are in order. With an even count, it is the average of the two middle values.
The mode is the value that appears most often.
Probability measures how likely something is, from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain). P(event) = favourable outcomes ÷ total outcomes.
What is the sum of angles in a triangle?
The angles of a triangle add up to 180°.
angles of a triangle add up to
What is the sum of angles in a quadrilateral?
The angles of a quadrilateral add up to 360°.
angles of a quadrilateral add up to
What is the sum of interior angles of a polygon?
For a polygon with n sides, the interior angles add up to (n − 2) × 180°. Each exterior angle of a regular polygon is 360° ÷ n.
In a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides: c² = a² + b². Example: 3² + 4² = 5².
An acute angle is less than 90°.
An obtuse angle is more than 90° but less than 180°.
A reflex angle is more than 180° but less than 360°.
Two angles are complementary if they add up to 90°.
Two angles are supplementary if they add up to 180°.
An equilateral triangle has all three sides equal and all three angles equal to 60°.
An isosceles triangle has two equal sides, and the angles opposite them are equal.
A scalene triangle has all three sides of different lengths.
A right-angled triangle has one angle of 90°. The side opposite it is the hypotenuse, the longest side.

A polygon is a closed flat shape made of straight sides: triangle (3), quadrilateral (4), pentagon (5), hexagon (6), heptagon (7), octagon (8), nonagon (9), decagon (10).
A quadrilateral is a shape with four sides, such as a square, rectangle, parallelogram, rhombus, trapezium or kite.
A rhombus has four equal sides; its opposite angles are equal and its diagonals cut each other at right angles.
A parallelogram has two pairs of parallel sides; opposite sides and opposite angles are equal.
A trapezium (trapezoid) is a quadrilateral with exactly one pair of parallel sides.
What is the radius of a circle?
The radius is the distance from the centre of a circle to its edge. The diameter is twice the radius.
What is the diameter of a circle?
The diameter is a straight line through the centre from one side of a circle to the other. It is twice the radius.
A chord is a straight line joining two points on a circle. The longest chord is the diameter.
An arc is part of the circumference of a circle.
What is a tangent to a circle?
A tangent is a line that touches a circle at exactly one point, and it is perpendicular to the radius at that point.
What is the value of pi?
π (pi) is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter: about 3.14159. In school problems 22/7 or 3.14 is often used.
What is the value of e?
e (Euler's number) is about 2.71828. It is the base of natural logarithms.

What is the value of root 3?
What is the formula for the area of a circle?
Area of a circle = πr², where r is the radius.
What is the formula for the circumference of a circle?
What is the formula for the area of a rectangle?
Area of a rectangle = length × breadth.
What is the formula for the perimeter of a rectangle?
What is the formula for the area of a square?
What is the formula for the perimeter of a square?
What is the formula for the area of a triangle?
Area of a triangle = ½ × base × height. With three sides a, b, c, use Heron's formula: √(s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)), where s = (a + b + c)/2.
What is the formula for the area of a parallelogram?
Area of a parallelogram = base × height.
What is the formula for the area of a trapezium?
Area of a trapezium = ½ × (sum of parallel sides) × height.
What is the formula for the area of a rhombus?
Area of a rhombus = ½ × d₁ × d₂ (product of the diagonals ÷ 2).
What is the formula for the volume of a cube?
Volume of a cube = side³. Total surface area = 6 × side².
What is the formula for the volume of a cuboid?
Volume of a cuboid = length × breadth × height. Total surface area = 2(lb + bh + hl).
What is the formula for the volume of a cylinder?
Volume of a cylinder = πr²h. Curved surface area = 2πrh. Total surface area = 2πr(r + h).
curved surface area of cylinder formula
What is the formula for the volume of a cone?
Volume of a cone = ⅓πr²h. Slant height l = √(r² + h²). Curved surface area = πrl. Total surface area = πr(l + r).
What is the formula for the volume of a sphere?
Volume of a sphere = ⁴⁄₃πr³. Surface area = 4πr².
What is the formula for the volume of a hemisphere?
Volume of a hemisphere = ⅔πr³. Curved surface area = 2πr². Total surface area = 3πr².
What is the formula for simple interest?
Simple interest = P × R × T ÷ 100, where P is the principal, R the rate % per year and T the time in years. Amount = P + SI.
What is the formula for compound interest?
Amount A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ for yearly compounding; compound interest = A − P. For compounding k times a year: A = P(1 + R/(100k))ᵏⁿ.
What is the formula for speed?
Speed = distance ÷ time. So distance = speed × time and time = distance ÷ speed. To change km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18.
What is the formula for profit percentage?
Profit % = (profit ÷ cost price) × 100, where profit = selling price − cost price. Loss % = (loss ÷ cost price) × 100.
What is the formula for the nth term of an AP?
nth term of an arithmetic progression: aₙ = a + (n − 1)d. Sum of n terms: Sₙ = n/2 × [2a + (n − 1)d].
What is the formula for the nth term of a GP?
nth term of a geometric progression: aₙ = a × rⁿ⁻¹. Sum of n terms: Sₙ = a(rⁿ − 1)/(r − 1) for r ≠ 1.
What is the formula for the sum of first n natural numbers?
1 + 2 + 3 + … + n = n(n + 1)/2. Sum of squares = n(n + 1)(2n + 1)/6. Sum of cubes = [n(n + 1)/2]².
sum of n natural numbers formula
The distance between (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂) is √((x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²).
The midpoint of (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂) is ((x₁ + x₂)/2, (y₁ + y₂)/2).
Slope m = (y₂ − y₁) ÷ (x₂ − x₁). The line is y = mx + c, where c is the y-intercept.
In a right triangle: sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse, cos θ = adjacent/hypotenuse, tan θ = opposite/adjacent. Also cosec = 1/sin, sec = 1/cos, cot = 1/tan.
sin²θ + cos²θ = 1; 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ; 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ; tan θ = sin θ / cos θ.
What are the laws of logarithms?
log(ab) = log a + log b; log(a/b) = log a − log b; log(aⁿ) = n log a; log_b b = 1; log_b 1 = 0; change of base: log_b a = log a / log b.
A logarithm answers 'what power?': log_b x = y means bʸ = x. For example, log₁₀ 1000 = 3 because 10³ = 1000.
n! (n factorial) is the product 1 × 2 × 3 × … × n. For example 5! = 120, and 0! = 1.
What is the formula for permutations and combinations?
Permutations (order matters): ⁿPᵣ = n!/(n − r)!. Combinations (order doesn't matter): ⁿCᵣ = n!/(r!(n − r)!).

How many zeros are in one million?
One million = 1,000,000 has 6 zeros; it equals 10 lakh.
How many zeros are in one billion?
One billion = 1,000,000,000 has 9 zeros; it equals 100 crore.

How many seconds are in a day?
How many days are in a leap year?
A leap year has 366 days (29 days in February). A normal year has 365 days.
How do you find a leap year?
A year is a leap year if it divides by 4, except century years, which must divide by 400. So 2024 and 2000 are leap years, but 1900 is not.
How many degrees are in a circle?
A dozen is 12. A score is 20, and a gross is 144 (12 dozen).
Roman numerals use letters: I = 1, V = 5, X = 10, L = 50, C = 100, D = 500, M = 1000. A smaller value before a bigger one is subtracted (IV = 4, IX = 9).

Srinivasa Ramanujan (1887–1920) was a self-taught Indian mathematician from Erode, Tamil Nadu, famous for his work on infinite series, number theory and continued fractions. India celebrates National Mathematics Day on 22 December, his birthday.
1729 is the Hardy–Ramanujan number: the smallest number that can be written as the sum of two cubes in two ways: 1³ + 12³ = 9³ + 10³.
Aryabhata (476–550 CE) was an Indian mathematician and astronomer who wrote the Aryabhatiya. He worked with place value and gave an accurate value of π. India's first satellite was named after him.
Zero as a number was developed in ancient India. Brahmagupta (628 CE) gave the first rules for calculating with zero.
Who is the father of geometry?
Euclid, the ancient Greek mathematician, is called the father of geometry. He wrote the Elements.
Who is the father of algebra?
Al-Khwarizmi, a Persian mathematician of the 9th century, is often called the father of algebra. The word 'algebra' comes from his book.
It is named after the Greek mathematician Pythagoras, but the idea was known earlier, including in India's Baudhayana Sulba Sutra.
